headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from ctx’s MCP/Claude Code hooks feeding MinerU’s document pipeline; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events and uses mcp/stdio, while MinerU exposes an MCP Server and processes Markdown/JSON/OCR text. That creates a plausible default bridge where attacker-controlled document content can be surfaced into ctx’s context and treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF ctx ingests MinerU output through MCP or Claude Code hooks without provenance tagging, injection is possible.
IF MinerU content is copied into ctx-managed prompts or logs, instruction-like text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MinerU outputs into ctx prompts.
Add provenance labels to all MinerU-derived text before ctx reads it.
Restrict ctx hooks to allowlisted event types only.
Review one sample document flow for instruction-like text handling.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement at the MCP boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU is documented as private/fully offline and lacks filesystem read/write privileges beyond local inputs, while ctx touches filesystem and logs. A leakage path exists only if they share a workspace or logs are copied between them; the pair does not show default third-party exfiltration from MinerU. Because the shared-storage assumption is not explicit, severity stays low.
conditions: IF ctx and MinerU share the same local workspace or log directory, MinerU outputs may be exposed to ctx.
IF ctx forwards audit/runtime logs containing document text, sensitive content can leak across the pair.
mitigations: Separate ctx and MinerU working directories.
Rotate or redact logs before sharing them between agents.
Disable document-text logging in ctx for MinerU runs.
Verify MinerU stays offline for the tested workflow.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can install packages and run browsers, while MinerU can use MCP and concurrent inference but cannot write files, modify git, or execute shells. Their write surfaces do not overlap in the profiles, so direct resource conflict is limited. The main risk is coordination friction through shared MCP or concurrent sessions, not destructive contention.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same MCP resource without locking, concurrent requests may interfere.
IF ctx installs packages into a shared environment while MinerU reads from that environment, state drift can occur.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate environment.
Avoid shared MCP resources unless locked.
Pin package versions for ctx runs.
Keep MinerU read-only with respect to shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add resource locking for shared MCP targets.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is a context-management harness that observes Claude Code events, and MinerU produces extracted document text, tables, and OCR. If MinerU output is fed into ctx and then into downstream actions without verification, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect tool use or decisions. The pairwise pathway is plausible by default but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF MinerU extraction output is treated as authoritative by ctx, downstream actions may inherit OCR or layout errors.
IF ctx forwards MinerU-derived facts into another agent or workflow without verification, errors cascade.
mitigations: Require human review of extracted facts before action.
Compare MinerU output against source documents for a sample set.
Mark OCR-derived fields as untrusted in ctx.
Limit downstream automation to high-confidence fields only.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any action-taking step.

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is described as private/fully offline and handles document formats that may contain regulated data, while ctx touches audit/runtime logs and GitHub/GitHub Actions APIs. The likely compliance issue is retention or residency mismatch if regulated documents or logs are moved into ctx’s cloud-connected surfaces. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by MinerU and then copied into ctx logs or GitHub-connected workflows, retention/residency obligations may be violated.
IF the operator stores document outputs in GitHub or GitHub Actions, compliance scope expands.
mitigations: Keep regulated documents out of GitHub-connected workflows.
Redact logs before exporting them from ctx.
Confirm whether the document class is subject to residency rules.
Use local-only storage for MinerU outputs.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention controls.
